title: The Dice Game: Draupadi Questions the Wager
subtitle: A challenge to the claim made in the council hall

wager.author: traditionally attributed to Vyasa
wager.locator: Book IV · DYUTA; Book IV · DYUTA, normalized characters 2126-2309
wager.excerpt: Doth a crowned king and husband stake his wife and lose his queen, Did my noble lord and monarch sense and reason lose at dice, Other stake he did not wager, wedded wife to sacrifice!
wager.note: Verbatim English translation from Dutt. The Mahabharata volume is a condensed verse rendering; the Ramayana volume contains only the Balakandam and Ayodhyakandam.

narrativeBlocks.title: A game that can't be won
narrativeBlocks.body: Yudhishthira — eldest Pandava, famously honest, hopelessly drawn to dice — is invited to a game in the Kaurava hall. The dice are Shakuni's, and they are loaded.

narrativeBlocks.title: Everything on the table
narrativeBlocks.body: He loses his wealth, his kingdom, his brothers one by one, himself — and finally, desperate, stakes Draupadi, their shared wife. She loses to a stranger's dice.

narrativeBlocks.title: Dragged into the hall
narrativeBlocks.body: Dushasana drags her by the hair into the assembly and tries to strip her — and the elders sit silent. Her sari, by divine mercy, extends endlessly, but the insult stands.

narrativeBlocks.title: The question nobody answers
narrativeBlocks.body: Draupadi asks the hall the question the epic never resolves: did Yudhishthira stake himself FIRST? If he lost himself before staking her, he had no right to stake her — a slave cannot wager what he no longer owns. The law stammers; no one answers.

narrativeBlocks.title: The vow that starts a war
narrativeBlocks.body: She takes oaths from the hall — Bhima will break Dushasana's thigh, drink his blood — and the humiliation is the debt the war later pays. The epic's darkest scene is legal, not violent.
